source_behavior.busy_state: _syncing blocks repeat interaction while the operation runs
source_behavior.history_follow_up: site operation history is reread in the finally path

security.site_ownership: sync mutation explicitly binds the site to active tenant; connection/history reads use tenant-scoped models
security.idempotency: one Idempotency-Key is generated per explicit user click and replay cannot duplicate the queued SyncSiteJob

retry_and_reconciliation.accepted_run: POST returns the durable SyncRun and reuses an in-flight run when one already exists
retry_and_reconciliation.polling: GET durable SyncRun until a terminal state or bounded timeout
retry_and_reconciliation.authoritative_success_reread: connection state and site operation history are fetched from the server after succeeded
retry_and_reconciliation.failure_reread: connection/history reread is attempted after failure while preserving the original synchronization error

coverage: source method and both source routes
exact canonical operation marker in production UI
same-key replay without duplicate SyncRun or job dispatch
frontend success only after durable SyncRun success and server reread
cancelled and cancel_requested states are failures

terminality.reason: The Site Connection Center Sync-now control now invokes the existing tenant-owned, idempotent queued WordPress synchronization path, observes the durable run to a truthful terminal result, and rereads authoritative connection plus operation history state before reporting success.
